Scaling Laws for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Reasoning Models

Shows MoE reasoning models follow distinct scaling laws with compute-optimal expert counts

https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01234

This MoE scaling laws paper is the most interesting arxiv drop this week — the compute-optimal expert count result contradicts the folk wisdom that more experts is always better https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01234v2
Worth reading skeptically: the MoE scaling paper's optimal-expert claim depends heavily on their FLOP accounting choices. Still a useful contribution. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.01234

A new biorxiv preprint reports a CRISPR base-editing approach that corrects the most common cystic fibrosis mutation in patient-derived organoids with 71% efficiency https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2026.08.01.123456v1

Impressive editing efficiency in the CF organoid preprint, but note the off-target analysis only covers 8 predicted sites. Orthogonal genome-wide assays would strengthen this. https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2026.08.01.123456v1.full

New in Nature: a global analysis finding that citation inequality has doubled since 1990, with the top 1% of papers absorbing an ever-growing share of citations https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-09876-1?utm_source=twitter
The citation inequality paper undersells the role of field growth — normalizing by field size shrinks the effect by half. Thread with reanalysis: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-09876-1
We are hiring two postdocs to study AI and work. Great team, great data. Apply here: https://apply.example.edu/postdoc
Conference deadline extended to Sept 1! Get those papers in https://mlconf.example.org/cfp
The MoE scaling laws paper also quietly shows dense models are compute-optimal below 3B params, which everyone is ignoring https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01234
the CF base editing preprint is exactly the kind of result that makes me optimistic about genetic medicine https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2026.08.01.123456v1
Excited about our lab retreat next week! Beautiful venue this year.

A new JAMA study of 45,000 patients finds GLP-1 receptor agonists associated with 22% lower incidence of major cardiovascular events in non-diabetics https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/10.1001/jama.2026.12345

Before you share the GLP-1 cardio study: it's observational, and the healthy-user bias here is likely substantial. The authors acknowledge this in the limitations. https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/10.1001/jama.2026.12345
